kind: local installed VSCodium Web lifecycle control

recordedEnvironment.source: Local registry/API/tool observations; editor native architecture is separately checked by PE header and extension host.

preparationHistory.name: run-01
preparationHistory.cause: Reusing source ZipInfo objects for output mutated their offsets before the unchanged-payload comparison read them again.
preparationHistory.fix: copy.copy(info) isolates output metadata; payload preservation regression verifies original and candidate bytes.

preparationHistory.name: unsafe-name unit case
preparationHistory.cause: Python on Windows normalizes ZIP backslashes before filename-based validation.
preparationHistory.fix: Validate original ZIP names (orig_filename); construct a raw backslash fixture after ZipInfo initialization.

runs.name: run-02
checks: Normally installed local candidate activates with exact owned module hashes and isolated loaded path
A source breakpoint binds and evaluates marker=40 through the installed native adapter
Two independent real Web sessions respond with distinct owned nonces and PIDs
A cycle 0: exact session terminates, PID exits, port rebinds and output/terminal queues clear while B survives
A cycle 1: exact session terminates, PID exits, port rebinds and output/terminal queues clear while B survives
A cycle 2: exact session terminates, PID exits, port rebinds and output/terminal queues clear while B survives
B final stop releases its exact PID, HTTP port and owned output

phases.label: verify installed local candidate
A initial installed-command launch and breakpoint
B independent installed-command launch
A cycle 0 targeted stop and owned cleanup
B preserved after A cycle 0
A cycle 1 dirty edit and installed-command retry
A cycle 1 targeted stop and owned cleanup
B preserved after A cycle 1
A cycle 2 dirty edit and installed-command retry
A cycle 2 targeted stop and owned cleanup
B preserved after A cycle 2
B final targeted stop and owned cleanup

runs.interpretation: Behavioral lifecycle assertions passed. Stop-time adapter errors remain recorded; this is not an error-free-log or release-qualification claim.
